saints.name: St. John
saints.title: Apostle and Evangelist
saints.shortBlurb: The beloved disciple who leaned on the Lord's breast, stood by the Cross, and wrote the fourth Gospel…
biography: John, son of Zebedee and Salome and brother of James the Greater, was called from his nets on the Lake of Galilee; Jesus named the brothers Boanerges, 'sons of thunder.' With Peter and James he belonged to the inner three, witnesses of the raising of Jairus's daughter, the Transfiguration, and the agony in Gethsemane.

He is 'the disciple whom Jesus loved': he leaned on the Lord's breast at the Last Supper, stood by the Cross and received the Mother of Jesus into his care, and outran Peter to the empty tomb, where he saw and believed.

In later years he governed the churches of Asia from Ephesus. Tertullian relates that under Domitian he emerged unharmed from a cauldron of boiling oil before the Porta Latina at Rome and was banished to Patmos, where he received the Apocalypse.

Tradition ascribes to him the fourth Gospel — written at Ephesus, says St. Irenaeus — three Epistles, and the Apocalypse. He died at Ephesus about 100, under Trajan, the only Apostle not to shed his blood, repeating, 'Little children, love one another.' He is patron of theologians, writers, and friendship.
saints.knownFor: The beloved disciple; author of the fourth Gospel.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 27 December
